title: Finding Disposition and Transfer
objective: Propagate canonical findings and eligible conditions through generated specs, slice briefs, PR evidence, and readiness gates without losing identity.
description: Adds a versioned governance manifest and validates exact-one transfer targets so every conditioned obligation remains traceable and enforceable downstream.
parallel_safe_reason: This slice consumes finalized decision records and changes shared spec generation and readiness gates.
must: Allow spec creation only from approved or eligible approved-with-conditions decisions.
Support individual finding transfer and batch disposition commands against the canonical governance store.
Validate all transfer targets before rendering or mutating generated artifacts.
Require every transferred finding target to resolve to exactly one existing phase or slice.
Preserve decision kind, approved artifact version and digest, reviewer recommendation, canonical finding ID, run and review origin, disposition, acceptance reference, target, and required evidence.
Generate one immutable digest-bound governance manifest as a projection of the canonical run store, never as a second writer.
Render slice briefs, PR evidence, and human or JSON views as projections of the manifest.
Generate a traceability matrix and expose pending findings in destination slices and PR templates.
Make check-slice and check-pr reject omitted, orphaned, unknown, stale, or unresolved conditions.
Apply common redaction before generation, persistence, rendering, and export.
acceptance: AC-11 is satisfied for complete identity-preserving transfer and referentially strict gates.
AC-13 is satisfied for shared condition projections across spec, slice, PR, and CLI surfaces.
AC-14 is satisfied for redaction on generated, rendered, persisted, and exported transfer surfaces.
Spec creation accepts unconditional approval and only eligible conditioned approval.
Individual transfer and batch disposition preserve identity and cannot silently remove a finding.
Every transfer target resolves exactly once before any generated artifact is published.
Manifest source digest mismatch or unavailable canonical parity fails closed.
Omitted, orphaned, unknown, stale, or unresolved conditions block the relevant slice or PR gate.
tests: node --test tests/lib/ai-spec-generator.test.js tests/lib/check-slice.test.js tests/commands/spec-create.test.js tests/commands/slice-namespace.test.js tests/commands/ai-pr.test.js tests/commands/findings.test.js
